title: Almost Monday Scores Second Alternative Airplay No. 1 With ‘No More Regrets’

body: Almost Monday earns its second No. 1 hit on Billboard ’s Alternative Airplay chart (dated Nov. 28) with “No More Regrets.” The song, released May 1 via Hollywood Records, rises two places to the summit thanks to a 5% increase in spins at the format Nov. 13-19, according to Luminate. (The Alternative Airplay chart measures songs’ weekly plays, as tabulated by Mediabase and provided to Billboard by Luminate, on 60 U.S. alternative radio stations.) The San Diego-based trio first led Alternative Airplay in February 2025 with “Can’t Slow Down,” a crossover hit that also reached No. 12 on Adult Pop Airplay and No. 24 on Pop Airplay. “No More Regrets” is Almost Monday’s eighth career Alternative Airplay entry. The group first made the ranking in October 2020 with “Broken People,” which reached No. 26. Earlier this year, “Lost” hit No. 18. title: Google gives publishers more visibility in AI Mode with new ‘Dive Deeper’ links
summary: Google wants curiosity to extend beyond AI-generated answers.
body: TL;DR Google has started rolling out its previously announced “Dive Deeper” section in Search’s AI Mode. The section displays prominent blue links, image thumbnails, and descriptions of related articles below AI-generated responses. The change aims to encourage further exploration of topics while giving publishers more visibility in AI-powered search results. Google’s efforts to turn Search into an answer engine have left publishers fighting for clicks and some users missing the depth that traditional search results offered. While AI Mode has made researching topics less time-consuming, Google recognizes that getting a quick answer isn’t always the end of someone’s search journey. To address this, the company is now rolling out a new “Dive Deeper” section in AI Mode to encourage readers to explore articles beyond its AI-generated answers. SEO consultant Glenn Gabe spotted and shared the change on X (via Search Engine Roundtable ). The section appears at the bottom of AI Mode responses and features prominent blue links, image thumbnails, and descriptions explaining what each article offers. It’s one of several improvements Google announced last month.

body: TL;DR Two unofficial apps bring notification and incoming call vibrations to the Fitbit Air. Cuff offers customizable alerts on Android, while AirBuzz uses iOS 27’s Shortcuts automations. Google designed the Fitbit Air for people who want to track their health without another screen competing for their attention. That philosophy explains why the band doesn’t display notifications or even vibrate when calls and messages arrive. But there’s a difference between avoiding constant distractions and wanting to know when something important needs your attention. Google hasn’t offered users that middle ground, so independent developers have stepped in. Two unofficial apps, Cuff for Android and AirBuzz for iOS, let the Fitbit Air buzz for incoming calls and notifications, giving owners a choice Google left out. As shared on Reddit (via Android Police ), Cuff reverse-engineers the tracker’s Bluetooth communication, letting users choose which alerts reach their wrists and customize how the band vibrates.
